result: For every finite ordinary tree T and every original leaf v with support s, coefficientwise deletion gives Delta_j(T) = Delta_j(T-v) + Delta_(j-1)(T-{v,s}) for every integer j under zero extension. Consequently, if x is the first strict descent of T, then for every original leaf v at least one of Delta_x(T-v) and Delta_(x-1)(T-{v,s}) is strictly negative. This is a rank-local alternative only; it does not imply Delta_p(T-v)<0 for p>=x+2.
proof: Partition independent sets according to whether they contain v. Since v is a leaf with support s, I_T(z)=I_(T-v)(z)+z I_(T-{v,s})(z). Taking the coefficient difference at j gives the displayed identity. If Delta_x(T)<0, its two integer summands cannot both be nonnegative.

exact_counterexample_to_unrestricted_tra.scope_warning: This disproves only the unguarded implication Delta_x(T)<0 => Delta_(x+2)(T-v)<0. It is outside the primary lower-region scope: 3p=9 is not less than 2alpha+1=7, and p is beyond alpha(T-v). It is not a primary counterexample.

literature_boundary.source: Ferenc Bencs, On trees with real rooted independence polynomial, arXiv:1703.05409 (2017), Propositions 3.3 and 3.4
literature_boundary.scope: The cited propositions establish real-rootedness for the n-centipede and n-caterpillar families defined in that paper. They do not state real-rootedness or unimodality for arbitrary trees and do not give a rank-transfer theorem for T-v.
literature_boundary.use: No theorem from this paper is used to infer a sign for the assigned general-tree selector.

primary_obligation_remaining: For eligible p with x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1, a useful transfer would require a new cross-rank bound connecting Delta_x(T) to Delta_p(T-v), or a direct proof about the strict selector. The deletion identity at rank x does not supply that bound. No such bound or eligible counterexample is established here.
